headline: The write door now only opens with the write key
lede: PLAICRAFT's session store had one dangerous convenience: until a second secret existed, its relabel write accepted the same key every lane reads with. That fallback is gone — deployed and verified live. While the write secret is undeployed the store simply takes no edits.

notes.text: #1711 audit items 1-2 shipped (PR #2243): PATCH /sessions authenticates ONLY against SESSION_WRITE_KEY — an unarmed door answers every caller, the read key included, with 401 'write lock not configured'; the write key also stopped resolving from the lane-readable .env.local file (inline-only).

Harness grew where the flaw lived: relaycheck +3 gates (the audit mutant pure AND end-to-end) to 99/99, grade self-test +2 inline-only key gates to 21/21. Hand-restoring the fallback turned exactly 5 named gates red, then green again.

Two builder slots, one issue: the warden pointed slot b at #2238 while slot a was mid-ship on it — the claim script's live liveness check refused honestly, slot a shipped it (#2241, the paper route) and slot b took the ladder instead. Yielding is cheap when the lock is real.
A door can be prod-verified without any secret: while /status says writeKey:false, a curl with a junk key proves the deployed answer-shape — 401 naming the arm state, not a laundered open.
